findings.title: canQuery no longer grants fallback for group-scoped view access
findings.body: canQuery() now is `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_USERS) || canView()`, but canView() only returns true for global view/manage roles or hasPermission at the Users resource level; it does not account for per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions. Previously an admin who can only view users of specific groups (via requireQuery in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource) might have been allowed to query based on group-scoped access, and is now blocked. This changes the admin's ability to list/search users they otherwise have group-scoped visibility into - search endpoints call requireQuery() before falling back to group-restricted search, so such admins would get a 403 instead of a filtered result set.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource.getId() names inconsistent with resource naming scheme (V1)
findings.body: In V1 GroupPermissions, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() strips the 'group.resource.' prefix off resource.getName() to produce a group id, consistent with getGroupResourceName(). This is fine for V1, but GroupPermissionsV2 (new file) instead adds groupResource.getId() (the resource's internal ID, not the group ID) to the granted set in its getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(). Since resources for V2 groups are created/named by group ID directly (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returning group.getId() as resource name), using resource.getId() instead of resource.getName() will return wrong values (internal resource UUIDs instead of actual group IDs), breaking downstream usages like UsersResource.searchForUser() and getUsersCount() that expect group IDs to filter users by UserModel.GROUPS attribute.
